name: CARBON COPIES
clue: Like diamond, this soft gray mineral that fills pencils is an allotrope of pure carbon

name: RUN FOR THE AGES
clue: This barefoot Ethiopian palace guard won the 1960 Olympic marathon on Rome's cobblestones, then won again in Tokyo wearing shoes.

name: FULL CIRCLE
clue: Killed in a Philippine island battle in 1521, he didn't live to complete the first circumnavigation his expedition finished

name: PERFECT SEASONS
clue: The 1972 edition of this NFL team went 17-0, the league's only unbeaten season capped by a Super Bowl win

name: CEILING THE DEAL
clue: Protesting that painting was not his art, this sculptor of 'David' spent 4 years frescoing a ceiling for Pope Julius II

name: OLYMPIC CITIES
clue: With the Games of 1908, 1948 and 2012, it became the first city to host the Summer Olympics three times

name: LOW POINTS
clue: Bathers bob like corks in this lake between Israel & Jordan, whose shore, about 1,400 feet below sea level, is Earth's lowest land

name: SCANDALOUS PREMIERES
clue: Fistfights broke out at the 1913 Paris premiere of this Stravinsky ballet about a pagan sacrifice

name: FIRST EMPERORS
clue: After unifying China in 221 B.C., he standardized script, coins, and axle widths; thousands of terracotta soldiers guard his tomb.

name: ELEMENT OF SURPRISE
clue: Spotted in the Sun's spectrum during an 1868 eclipse and named for a Greek god, it wasn't found on Earth until 1895

name: PROOF POSITIVE
clue: In 1931 this Austrian logician's incompleteness theorems proved that arithmetic contains true statements no formal proof can reach.

name: A DARK & STORMY NIGHT
clue: Subtitled 'The Modern Prometheus,' this novel sprang from an 1816 ghost-story contest at Lord Byron's villa on Lake Geneva

name: AND THE OSCAR GOES TO...
clue: This 1969 tale of two New York hustlers is the only X-rated film ever to win the Best Picture Oscar

name: BY ANY OTHER NAME
clue: Constantine renamed Byzantium for himself in 330 A.D.; since 1930 the city bridging the Bosporus has officially used this name

name: SHUTTER TO THINK
clue: Her 1936 photograph 'Migrant Mother', shot in a California pea-pickers' camp, became the defining image of the Great Depression.

name: CHEMICAL SYMBOLS
clue: Its symbol W comes from Wolfram, its German name; no metal melts at a higher temperature

name: LONG LIVE THE KING
clue: Becoming king at age four, this French monarch reigned 72 years, outliving both his son and his grandson

name: MEDICAL IMMORTALITY
clue: Cancer cells taken from this Virginia woman without her consent in 1951 became the first immortal human cell line, called HeLa.

name: FOR THE RECORD
clue: 'Mary had a little lamb' were the first words this Menlo Park inventor recited into his new phonograph in 1877

name: ROYAL READING
clue: Commissioned at the 1604 Hampton Court Conference, this English translation of scripture appeared 7 years later

name: VEXILLOLOGY
clue: Shaped like two stacked pennants, its banner is the only national flag that isn't a quadrilateral

name: FAB FOUR SOLO
clue: Though credited to the Beatles, this 1965 ballad features only Paul McCartney and a string quartet

name: MIDDLE OF NOWHERE
clue: Nicknamed for a Jules Verne captain, this oceanic 'pole of inaccessibility' is where space agencies aim their retiring spacecraft.

name: SCHOOL TIES
clue: Shakespeare enrolled this brooding prince at Wittenberg, the university town where Martin Luther posted his 95 theses

name: HIGH & DRY
clue: Astronomers prize the cloudless skies over this Chilean desert, the driest non-polar place on Earth and home to the ALMA observatory.

name: COLD WAR CHESS
clue: In Reykjavik in 1972, this American ended a 24-year Soviet grip on the world chess championship

name: LANGUAGE ISOLATES
clue: Spoken in the western Pyrenees, this European language has no known living relatives anywhere in the world

name: NOBEL LITERATURE
clue: In 1913 this Bengali poet of 'Gitanjali' became the first non-European to win the Nobel Prize in Literature

name: UNIFORM DECISION
clue: In 1997, 50 years after he broke in with Brooklyn, this pioneer's No. 42 was retired across every big-league clubhouse

name: UNITS OF MEASURE
clue: The SI unit of magnetic flux density honors this inventor, born in 1856 in what is now Croatia
